prompts.detail:
Create a carefully art-directed character finish and construction study sheet for the existing male and female heroes of this top-down 2D wuxia RPG. Reference 1 is the original character identity/proportion guide; reference 2 and 3 are approved-for-review concept direction only. Keep the original small readable chibi proportions and recognizable dark hair, warm red-brown robe with cream underlayer, sash, boots and existing weapons.
Lay out two full-body hero figures in front/three-quarter/back game views, plus large uncluttered close-up studies of: eye and hair silhouette; hair tied under a small headband and under a travel hat showing a clean occlusion seam; near/far hand gripping a short sword and a spear at different angles; robe sleeve, sash and layered hem; shoe, trouser cuff and grounded foot pivot. Use tidy leader lines or numbered marks from detail panels to the character; captions only as short readable labels. Show male and female anatomy/face as distinct but same-scale characters.
Handcrafted dark-fairytale storybook illustration with original visual language: lively tapered ink outlines, sparse fine hatching, matte watercolor/gouache, natural paper grain, subtle edge wear, asymmetrical cloth folds and believable weight. Limited palette of charcoal, warm vermilion, cream, weathered brown, muted jade. Detail must sharpen identity while keeping the silhouette crisp and readable at small game size. Inspired broadly by hand-inked gothic storybook games, never reproduce any specific game character, art, costume, logo, or UI.
Design-sheet only, not a game screenshot or sprite atlas. Clean breathing room, consistent anatomy, both hands visible where appropriate, accurate grip and foot contact. No detached floating layers, no extra fingers, no oversized ornamental armor, no photorealism, no glossy anime, no pixel art, no gibberish text.
prompts.motion:
Create a production-oriented motion keyframe concept sheet for the existing male and female top-down 2D wuxia RPG heroes. Reference 1 controls their identity, scale and default costume; reference 2 sets the hand-painted concept style. Keep the original chibi silhouette and short robe.
Show four clean horizontal strips, each strip divided into four evenly spaced key poses and a subtle loop arrow: male walk cycle, male run cycle, female walk cycle, female run cycle. Use one consistent three-quarter east/southeast game-facing direction across the strips so gait is easy to compare. Walk phases must read as contact, down, passing and up with low grounded steps; run phases as contact, compression, airborne/stride and recovery, with a more pitched torso and clear foot lift. Arms counter-swing naturally, hands and weapon stay coherent, and hair, sleeves and coat tails lag slightly behind the torso. Keep head scale, leg length, ground line, costume and lighting consistent across each cycle.
At far right, add small clean silhouette thumbnails for north, south, east and west run poses to indicate the cycle needs orientation-specific redraws; do not mirror the east-facing pose. Use thin arrows for travel direction and small ground contact marks, no ghosting clutter. Present a clear art direction key, not fake timing text.
Original hand-crafted dark-fairytale storybook game art: tapered imperfect ink lines, restrained crosshatching, matte gouache and watercolor on warm paper, earthy red-brown, charcoal, ivory and muted sage. Expressive but anatomically consistent. Broadly evocative of hand-drawn gothic storybook games but fully original, no copying known characters, assets, costumes, poses, trademarks or UI.
Not a sprite atlas, not a game screenshot. Each key pose must be distinct, feet should visibly plant when grounded, and no sliding implication or straight rigid arms. Keep the whole bodies visible, consistent in scale, and readable. Avoid extra limbs, malformed hands, pixel art, photorealism, glossy anime and illegible captions.
